title: Telemetry-driven regional routing & warm-standby priming checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a telemetry-driven orchestration layer that (1) selects target regions and tiers for failover with clear cost/latency trade-offs, (2) primes warm-standby fleets (cache + model variant prefetch) based on predicted acceptance score, and (3) verifies readiness using an automated checklist and scoring heuristic before cutover.

Motivation: previous manual warm-up steps and static region preference caused prolonged cutovers and higher error rates under load. We need deterministic readiness gating that is observable, reproducible, and integrates with routing policy engine.

Scope (this ticket):
- Define a readiness score composed of telemetry signals (KV cache hit rate, model variant checksum match, per-instance token latency p95, GPU memory pressure, queued inference backlog).
- Implement readiness agent (stateless probe) that runs on standby region to compute and publish the score to controller.
- Extend routing policy to consult readiness score with configurable thresholds per customer tier and per model variant.
- Add prefill actions: KV prefix prefetch, small synthetic generation to warm up kernels and KV cache, and optional low-rate shadow traffic to stabilize caches.
- Provide dashboard and alerting: readiness timeline, probe errors, and a post-cutover verification checklist.

Out of scope: full multi-region election algorithm (follow-on ticket), UI redesign for Console (separate PM story).
acceptance_criteria: Readiness agent publishes a numeric readiness_score (0-100) every 30s and is discoverable by the failover controller
Score components documented and weighted in a config file; weights are adjustable at runtime
Routing policy respects per-tenant thresholds: canary threshold, full-cutover threshold, and forced-cutover override with audit log
Prefill actions executed automatically and can be toggled per run; CPU/GPU impact capped by policy
Dashboard shows readiness history, component breakdown, and last 6 probe runs; pager triggers when score remains below canary threshold for >5 minutes during a cutover run

End-to-end chaos test: simulated zone outage triggers cutover candidate selection, readiness agent primes Standby A, controller waits until readiness_score >= full-cutover threshold, then initiates traffic migration; metrics validate <2 min additional downtime vs baseline
design_notes:
Readiness score composition: start with a compact set to avoid noisy signals. Proposed initial formula (weights editable):
- KV cache warmness (30%) — measured as fraction of expected prefixes present in LRU snapshot and recent hit rate on synthetic prefixes.
- Kernel warm latency delta (25%) — delta between warmed synthetic inference p95 and cold baseline p95.
- Instance-level latency p95 under a lightweight pressure test (20%).
- Queued backlog / available concurrency headroom (15%).
- Model variant integrity (10%) — checksum and tokenizer match confirmation.

Trade-offs:
- More signals => better precision but higher probe overhead. Start conservative and expand.
- Shadow traffic is the most realistic warm-up but has data/IO costs; use limited synthetic generations first.
- Prefill write-ops for KV must be rate-limited to avoid thrashing eviction policies on small fleets.

Telemetry plumbing: use existing metrics pipeline (prometheus -> pushgateway for ephemeral probes) and a lightweight readiness topic in our events bus. Controller will sample readiness events and persist short-lived readiness_runs with TTL 1 hour.

Security: prefill and synthetic requests must not log customer payloads. Use synthetic deterministic prompts generated from templates. Apply KMS access pattern used by other probe jobs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal): enable readiness agent and routing checks for a single test tenant in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Monitor dashboard and run cutover rehearsals during low-traffic windows.
Phase 2 (limited customers): open to P1 customers and QA fleets, collect feedback, tune thresholds.
Phase 3 (gradual): enable across region pairs and wire into automated runbooks for SRE. Use feature flag with percentage rollout.

Emergency override: manual 'force cutover' option requires 2-person approval and emits an audit event.
tests: Unit tests: score calculator edge cases, checksum mismatch handling, weight update application
Integration: readiness agent -> events bus -> controller; verify TTL and backpressure behavior
Load: confirm probe overhead under 1000 standby instances won't exceed 5% CPU on controller ingestion path
Chaos runbook: scripted zone failure, validate that controller waits appropriately and only routes when threshold met
Security review: ensure synthetic prompts and prefill flows do not surface customer data

2026-03-06 - Lena Voss: Implementing probe skeleton. Hit an edge with model variant checksum timing; moving checksum to happen immediately after model load completion event.
